sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph, including the ancient group’s campaign and defeat near Aquae Sextiae in 102 BCE.
Sections 1 and 2. Carolingian and Ottonian imperial title, geographic extent, development of the imperial designation and the problem of territorial authority.
Translated charter, preamble and clauses 1–7. Residential wall, annual payment of three and a half pounds, harbour trade, cemetery, visiting Jews, judicial jurisdiction.
Opening account of the 1084 settlement and the section Erste Pogrome, Kreuzzüge und die Pest. Attack of 1096 and the intervention of Bishop Johann.
Timeline on pp. 16–17, especially completion by 1146 and the 1182 privileges governing access, duties and maintenance.

Chapter III.1.b, Tätigkeitsbereich des Brückenmeisters, pp. 22–23 and notes 62–65. Petition of the citizens and Herbord, exemptions from toll, twelve-foot exclusion zone, divided fines, bishop and duke.
West choir overview, captions for Thimo von Kistritz and his seven villages, Hermann and Reglindis, Ekkehard II and Uta; caption dating of figures c. 1245–1250.
Uta among the twelve founders; anonymous sculptor, western choir completed around 1250 and later reception of Uta’s image.
Geographical data, property 1470rev; N51° 9′ 17.3″ and E11° 48′ 14.4″.
AT-OeStA/HHStA UR AUR 9228. Dates and places, regest, extent and seal description: only the Nuremberg part of this copy bears a golden seal of 66.6–67.2 mm in diameter.
Introduction and chs. 1–4. Seven electors, meeting at Frankfurt, voting, confirmation of electors’ rights and precedence.
Panel Die Goldene Bulle. Chapters 1–23 at Nuremberg and 24–31 at Metz in 1356, name from the gold seal, surviving original copies.
pp. 365–366, especially n. 46 quoting ch. 31. Languages for lay electoral heirs, age requirements, Latin and the interpretation of the Slavic language as Czech.
Ch. 31, two final paragraphs. Early language instruction for the four lay electoral families and the choice between sending children away and engaging experienced teachers at home.

labels.de: Teutonen – Wer durfte auf der Regensburger Brücke Geld verlangen?
labels.en: Teutons – Who could charge a fee on the bridge at Regensburg?

labels.de: 1084 · Rüdigers Rechte für die jüdische Gemeinde
labels.en: 1084 · Rüdiger grants rights to the Jewish community

summary.de: Bischof Rüdiger regelt Handel, Begräbnis und Gerichtsbarkeit für jüdische Familien. Der Stadtpunkt liegt am Rhein und verzeichnet den Geltungsort des Privilegs.
summary.en: Bishop Rüdiger grants trading, burial and judicial rights to Jewish families in Speyer. The city marker identifies where the grant applied.

labels.de: 26. September 1182 · Herbords Brücke wird vor Pflichtzöllen geschützt
labels.en: 26 September 1182 · Herbord’s bridge is protected from compulsory tolls

summary.de: Auf Bitten der Bürger und des Brückenmeisters sichert Friedrich I. den freien Übergang über die Donau und freie Zufahrten zu. Freiwillige Beiträge zum Unterhalt bleiben möglich.
summary.en: At the request of the citizens and the bridge master, Frederick I guarantees passage across the Danube without compulsory toll and clear approaches. Voluntary contributions can support maintenance.

labels.de: Um 1250 · Die Stifter werden in Stein sichtbar
labels.en: Around 1250 · The founders are commemorated in stone

summary.de: Im Naumburger Westchor erinnern zwölf Figuren an Wohltäter, die rund zwei Jahrhunderte vorher lebten. Die Station datiert die Arbeit der Bildhauer.
summary.en: Twelve figures in the west choir at Naumburg commemorate benefactors who lived some two centuries earlier. The station dates the sculptors’ work.

labels.en: 10 January 1356 · Issuing the electoral law at Nuremberg

summary.de: Karl IV. erlässt die ersten 23 Kapitel der Goldenen Bulle. Sie bestimmen Frankfurt am Main als Wahlort. Der Punkt zeigt die Stadt der Ausfertigung.
summary.en: Charles IV issues the first 23 chapters of the Golden Bull. They designate Frankfurt am Main for elections. The point marks the issuing town.

labels.de: 25. Dezember 1356 · Die Metzer Bestimmung über Sprachen
labels.en: 25 December 1356 · The Metz provision on languages

summary.de: Die Schlusskapitel der Goldenen Bulle entstehen in Metz. Kapitel 31 regelt die sprachliche Erziehung der Erben der vier weltlichen Kurfürsten.
summary.en: The final chapters of the Golden Bull are issued at Metz. Chapter 31 deals with language education for the heirs of the four lay electors.

summary.de: Jüdische Familien in Speyer, ein Brückenmeister in Regensburg und zwei Frauen in einem Domchor zeigen, wer im mittelalterlichen Reich Rechte besaß und wessen Namen erhalten blieben.
summary.en: Jewish families in Speyer, a bridge master in Regensburg and two women in a cathedral choir reveal who could claim rights in the medieval Empire and whose names survived.
